full_text_en:
Chen Yongjun Embezzlement Case

Defendant: Chen Yongjun, male, 27 years old, formerly a cashier at Shimen County Chemical Fertilizer Plant, Hunan Province, arrested on December 5, 1991.

Defense Counsel: Qin Shixi and Guo Xiaohui, lawyers from Shimen County Law Firm.

The Changde City People's Procuratorate of Hunan Province initiated a public prosecution against the defendant Chen Yongjun for the crime of corruption, and submitted the case to the Changde Intermediate People's Court. After public trial, the Changde Intermediate People's Court found the following facts:

During his tenure as a cashier at the Shimen Chemical Fertilizer Plant, from May 1988 to November 1991, the defendant Chen Yongjun, taking advantage of his position, committed 62 separate acts by means such as failing to record income, secretly withdrawing the plant's funds from the bank, and misappropriating funds under his control, thereby embezzling public funds totaling RMB 175,651.94. Later, fearing exposure of his crimes, he destroyed some documents and absconded with public funds of over RMB 54,000 before being apprehended. After the case was solved, a total of RMB 96,769.22 in illicit money and goods were recovered, resulting in a loss of RMB 78,882.72. Among the embezzled funds, Chen Yongjun squandered over RMB 67,000 on purchases, entertainment, and gifts, and over RMB 11,000 lent to others had not yet been recovered.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including product sales invoices, account clearance documents, bank account books, transfer checks, appraisal reports on accounting records, documents, and seals, as well as witness testimony and the recovered illicit money and goods. The defendant Chen Yongjun also made confessions.

On March 3, 1994, the Changde Intermediate People's Court of Hunan Province rendered a criminal judgment finding the defendant Chen Yongjun guilty of corruption, sentencing him to death, and depriving him of political rights for life. Chen Yongjun appealed to the Hunan Higher People's Court. The grounds for appeal were: First, the first-instance criminal judgment erroneously treated as corruption the payments collected by others using his seal, as well as amounts for which it had not been ascertained whether the purchasers had paid. Second, the public funds he lent to others should be characterized as misappropriation of public funds, which should carry a lighter penalty than corruption. Chen Yongjun's defense counsel argued that the first-instance criminal judgment failed to account for the whereabouts of over RMB 40,000 in illicit funds, rendering the facts unclear; that the seizure of Lu Bin's vehicle should have been set off against the embezzled funds Chen Yongjun had lent to Lu Bin, but was not; and that Chen Yongjun's ability to embezzle public funds was due to serious dereliction of duty by the plant's leadership, which the first instance failed to consider, thus the sentence was too harsh, and a lenient punishment was requested.

The Hunan Higher People's Court affirmed the facts of Chen Yongjun's crime as determined by the first-instance court. The court held that the appellant Chen Yongjun, as a person who handled and managed public property, took advantage of his position to embezzle public funds. His conduct violated Article 1 of the Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Concerning the Punishment of Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery (hereinafter "Supplementary Provisions"), constituting the crime of corruption, and should be punished under Article 2(1) of those Supplementary Provisions. The appellant Chen Yongjun's first ground of appeal was found inconsistent with the facts upon examination. First, in all cases where others collected payments on his behalf, the sales invoices bore the seals of the collectors, and no instance was found where the flat seal of "Chen Yongjun" was used to collect payments. Second, except for one instance where there was evidence that the payment collected by another person had been transferred to Chen Yongjun and was thus found to be embezzlement, no other such instances were determined as embezzlement. Third, according to attendance records, all the dates on which the original judgment found Chen Yongjun to have embezzled sales proceeds were dates when Chen Yongjun was on duty. Fourth, for all amounts found to have been embezzled by Chen Yongjun, purchasers confirmed that payment had been made in full; amounts for which purchasers could not confirm payment or for which there was no other evidence of full payment were not determined to have been embezzled by Chen Yongjun. The appellant Chen Yongjun's second ground of appeal was also found untenable upon examination. If the funds had been misappropriated, there would be corresponding entries in the accounts and complete accounting vouchers, indicating that although the public funds had been misappropriated, the misappropriator still recognized them as public funds. However, the facts showed that before absconding, Chen Yongjun not only took a large amount of public funds with him but also destroyed documents such as the accounting copies of sales invoices under his custody and check stubs for cash withdrawals. This conduct sufficiently demonstrated that Chen Yongjun had regarded these public funds as private property he could exclusively possess. The first-instance court had already accounted for the full whereabouts of the over RMB 78,000 in losses caused by Chen Yongjun's embezzlement. The vehicle seized from Lu Bin had been determined to belong to the Shimen County Material Trade Center and should be returned to that entity, not set off against the embezzled funds Lu Bin owed Chen Yongjun. Although Chen Yongjun committed the crime by taking advantage of the serious dereliction of duty by the plant's leadership, the duration of his criminal activities was long and the amount involved was huge, constituting a particularly serious case, and the death penalty was legally warranted. The defense counsel's request for a lenient punishment for Chen Yongjun was not accepted. Based on the above facts, the first-instance court legally sentenced him to death and deprived him of political rights for life. The facts were clearly found, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, the conviction was accurate, the sentence was appropriate, and the trial procedure was lawful.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 136(1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Hunan Higher People's Court ruled on June 9, 1994: To dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

Pursuant to Article 144 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the Hunan Higher People's Court submitted the Chen Yongjun corruption case to the Supreme People's Court for review.

After review, the Supreme People's Court held that the facts of the crime as determined by the first and second instances were clearly found, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, and the trial procedure was lawful. During the period when this case was submitted for review, the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Concerning the Punishment of Crimes Against the Company Law (hereinafter "Decision") had been promulgated and come into effect. The defendant Chen Yongjun, as an employee of a state-owned enterprise, took advantage of his position to embezzle public funds. Before the Decision came into effect, this conduct should have been determined as the crime of corruption in accordance with Article 1 of the Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Concerning the Punishment of Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery, and should have been punished under Article 2 of those Supplementary Provisions. Article 10 of the Decision separately stipulated the conduct of employees of a company who, taking advantage of their positions or work, embezzle company property, as the crime of embezzlement. Article 14 provided that the Decision also applied to employees of enterprises other than limited liability companies and joint-stock companies who committed the crime of embezzlement. The penalty for the crime of corruption was heavier than that for the crime of embezzlement. In accordance with Article 9 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, where the new law does not consider the conduct a crime or imposes a lighter penalty, the new law shall apply. Accordingly, the Supreme People's Court rendered the following judgment on March 26, 1996:

1. The criminal judgment and criminal ruling of the Changde Intermediate People's Court of Hunan Province and the Hunan Higher People's Court in this case are hereby set aside.

2. The defendant Chen Yongjun is found guilty of the crime of embezzlement and sentenced to ten years' imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for two years.
